instructions: Fill a large bowl with cold water and squeeze in the juice of half the lemon.
Cut the top and bottom off the celery root. Stand it on a flat end and slice off the peel with a sharp knife, following the curve.
Cut the celery root into thin slices, then stack the slices and cut them into thin matchsticks. Transfer the matchsticks into the lemon water as you go.
In a second large bowl, stir 3/4 cup mayonnaise with 1 tbsp Dijon mustard and the juice of the other half of the lemon until smooth.
Drain the celery root and pat it dry with paper towels. Add it to the dressing with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper, and toss until every piece is coated.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. It keeps for 3 days in the fridge, so it works for lunches made ahead.
Pick the leaves from a few parsley sprigs. Taste the salad. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve cold, topped with the parsley leaves and a little black pepper.
method_notes: The Side Smith (the lead, 5.0 from 68 ratings) and Pardon Your French agree on matchsticks of raw celery root in a mustard mayonnaise, with lemon to keep it from browning and time in the fridge. They differ on extras: Pardon Your French adds cornichons and capers and chills 2 hours, the lead keeps it to mayonnaise, Dijon, lemon and parsley, which is what is written here. The lead's optional splash of milk is left out to keep the dish dairy-free.
